title: Your first week checklist
when: The things to get done in your first five working days so courses, systems and your plan are not held up later.

steps.d: Ask what your local certification goal is, who your Contracting Master Gunner (KMG) is, and who your mentor will be.
Make sure your position is coded for the Contracting functional area and your start date is right in your acquisition record. Your 36-month clock depends on it.

steps.t: Get your CAC, email and certificates working
steps.d: You need them for every system that follows.
Your supervisor's email address must be right or your training requests will stall.

steps.t: Log in to the WarU learning system and check your transcript
steps.d: Look for courses you may already have. Save a copy of the transcript.
Ask which systems your office uses (PIEE, SAM.gov, ACWS or PD2, VCE, GFEBS) and submit every role request this week.
List the five courses, the exam and target dates, and send it to your supervisor.
Pick the earliest class you can attend full time. See the course registration checklist.

steps.t: Build your plan in B2B Exam Prep
steps.d: Home, then three questions. Print it or add the dates to your calendar.
Begin with the Guiding Principles lessons and the FAR part titles flashcards.

tips: Write down every login, office phone number and point of contact in one place.
Ask to sit with a contract specialist for a day to see real actions.
watch: Do not wait for someone to request your system access for you.
Never share your CAC PIN or let someone use your login.
verify: Systems and onboarding steps differ by office.

title: Register for a WarU course (Army)
who: You, your supervisor and your KMG
when: Any time you need a certification course, such as CON 1100V or CON 1200V.

steps.t: Find the course in the WarU iCatalog
steps.d: Search the course number, open the course page and read the prerequisites.
Use Check Schedule. Write down the class number and dates. Make sure you finish any prerequisite before the class starts.
Go to the Student area and choose Apply for Training.

steps.t: Choose the course and class, and submit
steps.d: Double-check the class dates and your supervisor's email before you submit.
They approve in AITAS. A quick heads-up speeds it up.

steps.t: Watch for the training approval and your reservation email
steps.d: Approved requests flow through ATRRS to WarU.
It arrives about 25 days before class with links, pre-work and technical checks.

steps.t: Do the pre-work and test your equipment
steps.d: Camera, microphone and the class software, on the computer you will use.
Virtual classes are full time. Ask your supervisor to cover your workload.

steps.t: Mark the course in B2B Exam Prep
steps.d: Courses, then set My status to Signed up; set Done when you finish.

tips: Apply for the next course as soon as you know the current one's dates.
Keep every completion certificate in one folder.
watch: Missing a prerequisite can get you dropped from the class.
Dropping late can cost your unit and the next student a seat.
verify: AITAS screens and routing differ by organization. Ask your Contracting Master Gunner (KMG).

title: Sign up for and schedule CON 3990V
time: 30 minutes, then up to 90 days to test
who: You, your supervisor and your KMG
when: When you have finished your courses and CON 3910 and score 75% or better on practice exams.

steps.d: Apply like a course. You must be coded in contracting and have your supervisor's approval.
Your supervisor approves, then your organization's training approver in AITAS (your KMG knows who that is). The approval flows through ATRRS to WarU.

steps.t: Find the Authorization to Test email
steps.d: Pearson sends it within about 24 hours. Check junk mail.
Use the WarU page at pearsonvue.com/us/en/waru.html. Your name must match your ID exactly.
Test centers are recommended. You have 90 days from authorization to test.
No confirmation email means the booking did not finish. Go back and complete it.

steps.t: Record the date in B2B Exam Prep
steps.d: Certification 101, The exam, My exam date.
Two full exam simulations, a review of every miss, and the FAR part titles every day.
Government photo ID, arrive early, about 72 seconds per question, answer everything.
Certification 101, The exam, Record a result. A pass shows on your WarU transcript.

tips: Reschedule instead of canceling: rescheduling at least 48 hours ahead does not use an attempt.
Inside 48 hours, have your supervisor email scheduling@waru.edu.
watch: A no-show counts as a failed attempt and costs the Government a seat fee.
OnVUE online testing usually does not work on government computers.

title: Apply for your certification
when: When all five courses, the exam and 12 months of experience are done.

steps.d: WarU transcript showing the five courses, your exam result (transcript or Pearson score report), and a record of your experience.

steps.t: Review your experience with your supervisor
steps.d: Use the Experience checklist in Certification 101. Your supervisor confirms you have done a representative sample of contracting work.

steps.t: Submit the request through your component's process
steps.d: In the Army this runs through the Army DACM Office's systems (CAMP). Your KMG will show you the screen.
Track the request until it is approved, then save a copy of the certification.
Make sure your acquisition record and IDP show the certification.
80 hours every 2 years, at least 40 on contracting topics recommended.

tips: Keep a running folder of certificates from day one so this takes minutes, not days.
watch: Do not wait until month 35. Waivers take time.
verify: Certification request steps differ by component and change over time. Confirm the current Army process with your Contracting Master Gunner (KMG).

title: Run a simplified commercial buy (RFQ to award)
who: Contract specialist, for the contracting officer's signature
when: A commercial requirement above the micro-purchase threshold and at or below the SAT.

steps.d: Clear requirement, certified funds of the right type and year, and the right approvals.

steps.t: Check required sources and existing contracts
steps.d: AbilityOne, FPI, existing BPAs and IDIQs first (FAR Part 8).

steps.t: Do market research and decide on a set-aside
steps.d: Apply the rule of two and document the decision (FAR 19.104-1).
Above $20,000, post a notice on SAM.gov unless an exemption applies; at or below the SAT, posting the solicitation for electronic response can serve (FAR 5.101).
Use the commercial clauses and ask for quotes from at least three sources when practicable (FAR 12.201-1).
Share answers with everyone; amend the RFQ if something changes.
Use the basis stated in the RFQ. No formal plan or competitive range is needed (FAR 12.203).
Document the comparison; check SAM registration and exclusions.

steps.t: Prepare the award and file documentation
steps.d: Write down the procedures used and the number of quotes received (FAR 12.204).

steps.t: Contracting officer signs; distribute and report
steps.d: Send the order, notify others as required, and report the action.

tips: Templates in your contract writing system save time; still read every clause they insert.
watch: Do not split a requirement to stay under a threshold.
Do not award to a vendor that is not registered in SAM.

title: Document a fair and reasonable price
when: Every award and every priced modification.

steps.d: Competing quotes, prior prices paid, catalog or published prices, the IGCE and market research.
Adjust for time (inflation), quantity, delivery terms and differences in what was bought.
Competition and prior prices come first (FAR 15.404-1).
Look for items far above or below the others (FAR 15.404-6).
State the technique, the numbers, the adjustments and the conclusion in a short memo.
Ask the vendor for an explanation or negotiate before deciding.

tips: A one-paragraph memo written at the time beats a perfect memo written for an auditor later.
watch: Comparing with the IGCE alone when real market prices exist.

title: Do and document market research
when: Before writing a new requirement, and before soliciting above the SAT.

steps.t: Define what you need to learn
steps.d: Commercial availability, number and size of sources, typical prices, terms and how industry sells it.

steps.t: Search prior buys and existing contracts
steps.d: Your office's records, other agencies, and contract data in SAM.gov.
SAM.gov entity search, GSA Advantage, company websites and catalogs.
Post a sources sought notice or RFI, or hold an industry day, sharing the same information with everyone.
The customer, the small business professional and other contracting offices.
Commercial or not, set-aside or not, contract type and method.
What you searched, whom you contacted, what you found and what you concluded (FAR 10.001).

watch: Do not share the IGCE or one company's information.
Do not let the incumbent shape the requirement.

title: Handle an unauthorized commitment
who: The person who made the commitment, the contracting office, legal and the ratifying official
when: Someone without authority promised a vendor payment and the vendor performed.

steps.t: Do not just pay the invoice
steps.d: A new order to cover it hides the problem. Ratification is the required route.

steps.t: Get a written statement from the person who made the commitment
steps.d: What happened, when, why, and what was received.

steps.t: Collect the vendor's invoice and proof of delivery
steps.d: The Government must have received the goods or services.
Funds must have been available at the time of the commitment.
It must be fair and reasonable.

steps.t: Check that the contract would otherwise have been proper
steps.d: Same rules as a normal award.
Legal counsel concurs as agency procedures require.
The HCA, delegable no lower than the chief of the contracting office (FAR 1.405(b)(2)).

steps.t: If ratified, issue the contract action
steps.d: Pay the vendor through a proper contract.
Brief the unit on who can commit the Government.

watch: Ratification is not automatic; if denied, the vendor may need other remedies.
The person who made the commitment may face discipline.

title: Process a modification
who: Contract specialist, for the contracting officer's signature
when: Any change to an awarded contract: funding, an option, a change order or an agreed adjustment.

steps.d: Administrative change, change order, supplemental agreement or option exercise (FAR 43.203).
Is the change within the general scope? If not, it is new work.

steps.t: Get funds first if cost goes up
steps.d: No modification that adds cost without available funds (FAR 43.205).

steps.t: For priced changes, get a proposal and analyze it
steps.d: Price analysis or cost analysis, then negotiate.
Price negotiation memorandum or a short memo, plus any required approvals.
Clear description, changes to price and schedule, and the authority cited.

steps.t: Get the contractor's signature when bilateral
steps.d: Supplemental agreements need both signatures.
Then report the action and update the file.

watch: Letting a COR's direction become the modification after the fact.
Leaving out the release of claims language on an agreed adjustment when your office requires it.

title: Exercise an option
who: Contract specialist, with the COR and customer
when: A contract option period or quantity is coming due.

steps.d: Many contracts require preliminary written notice by a set date. Calendar it.
Ask the customer in writing.
Funds must be available before exercise.
The contractor must not be excluded.
Performance must be acceptable; check CPARS and the COR's reports.

steps.t: Confirm the option is the best way to meet the need
steps.d: Compare the option price with current market prices.

steps.t: Confirm the option was evaluated at award
steps.d: Options not evaluated in the original competition need other authority.

steps.t: Document the determination and issue the modification
steps.d: Unilateral SF 30 within the time the contract allows (FAR 17.204-1).

watch: Missing the exercise deadline means the option is gone.

title: Close out a firm-fixed-price contract
when: All deliveries accepted or services performed, and no options remain.

steps.d: Deliveries accepted, services performed, options expired.
Check that all invoices are paid in WAWF.
Government property returned or disposed of.
Coordinate with the resource manager so the customer can reuse them.
Fair, factual and specific.
Use your office's closeout checklist.

steps.t: Close the file in the system of record
steps.d: In the Army, the VCE Paperless Contract File.

tips: Close simplified buys as soon as delivery and payment are confirmed.
watch: Old unliquidated obligations are audit findings and can mean canceled funds.

title: Find something in the FAR fast
when: Someone asks 'where does it say that?' or you need the rule behind a decision.

steps.d: Competition, small business, pricing, changes, protests, and so on.
Use the part titles: Part 6 competition, 19 small business, 15 negotiation, 43 modifications, 33 protests.

steps.t: Use the RFO pages for DoW work
steps.d: acquisition.gov's FAR Overhaul pages show the text DoW uses; the codified FAR may show old numbers.
DFARS (FAR part + 200), then PGI for how-to, then AFARS (FAR part + 5100).
Your command may add procedures.
Regulation, part, section, paragraph. Note the date you checked.

tips: Learn the part titles; they are your map.

title: What to do when a protest arrives
who: Contracting officer and legal counsel, with your help
when: A protest is filed with the agency or GAO.

steps.t: Tell your contracting officer and legal counsel at once
steps.d: Note how and when the protest arrived.
Was it filed within 10 days of award or 5 days after a required debriefing? If so, performance must be suspended unless overridden (FAR 33.104-3, 33.105).
The full file, notes, emails and evaluator materials. Delete nothing.

steps.t: Do not discuss it outside proper channels
steps.d: No side conversations with the protester or awardee.
GAO expects the agency report within 30 days.
If there is a real mistake, fixing it quickly is often best.

watch: Letting performance continue after a timely protest without an approved override.
